content: Progesterone is a hormone that plays a critical role in supporting pregnancy and maintaining reproductive health. It is commonly used in various forms, including vaginal suppositories, to help women achieve and sustain pregnancy, particularly in cases of infertility or assisted reproductive technology (ART) treatments. Dosage and Administration: For women with partial or complete ovarian failure, a dose of 90 mg (8% gel) is administered intravaginally once daily. Alternatively, 90 mg may be used twice daily intravaginally. Treatment may continue for 10-12 weeks post-conception until placental autonomy is established. In cases where a lower dose (45 mg, 4% gel) administered every other day for six doses does not elicit a response, the higher dose of 90 mg (8% gel) every other day for six doses may be attempted. Progesterone vaginal inserts should not be used concurrently with other vaginal products, such as antifungal medications, as this may interfere with the release and absorption of progesterone. Side Effects: Common side effects include: Breast enlargement (40%) and tenderness (27%) Drowsiness (27%) Abdominal cramps (15-26%) Mood swings (22-23%) Nausea (6-22%) Depression (11-19%) Dizziness (15-24%) Sleep disturbances (18%) Perineal pain (17%) Nervousness (16%) Urinary difficulties (11%) Musculoskeletal pain (12%) Headache (13%) Breast pain (13%) Abdominal pain (5-12%) Constipation (2-3%) Vaginal discharge (10%) Fatigue, irritability, and diarrhea (7-8%) Rare but serious side effects include blood clots (e.g. If any of these occur, the medication should be discontinued immediately. Precautions: Progesterone therapy is contraindicated in individuals with known or suspected breast or genital malignancies, active thromboembolic disorders, severe liver disease, undiagnosed abnormal vaginal bleeding, or a history of missed abortion or ectopic pregnancy. Caution is advised in patients with a family history of breast cancer, deep vein thrombosis (DVT), or pulmonary embolism (PE), as well as those with conditions such as endometriosis, diabetes, hypertension, renal or hepatic impairment, or diseases exacerbated by fluid retention (e.g., migraines, epilepsy, or asthma). Physicians should monitor for early signs of thrombotic disorders, such as thrombophlebitis, cerebrovascular events, or retinal thrombosis. If these occur, treatment should be stopped immediately. A thorough physical examination, including breast and pelvic exams and a Pap smear, should be conducted before initiating therapy. Use During Pregnancy and Lactation: Progesterone is generally considered safe during pregnancy when used as directed by a healthcare provider. However, it should only be used under medical supervision. The medication passes into breast milk, so caution is advised for breastfeeding mothers. Drug Interactions: Progesterone may interact with other medications, altering their effectiveness or increasing the risk of side effects. Patients should inform their healthcare provider of all medications and supplements they are taking. Avoid using other vaginal products within six hours before or after progesterone administration. Storage and Handling: Store at room temperature and keep away from moisture and heat. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet or pour it into drains. Dispose of it properly when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Notes: Progesterone therapy should be used for the shortest duration necessary to achieve the desired effect. It is not recommended for the prevention of dementia or vascular disease in postmenopausal women, as it may increase the risk of these conditions when combined with estrogen. Patients with a history of depression should be closely monitored during treatment. Progesterone is a natural progestin hormone that supports mammary gland development, induces changes in the endometrium, relaxes uterine smooth muscles, and maintains pregnancy. It is metabolized primarily in the liver and excreted through urine and feces. Its half-life ranges from 5 to 20 minutes, and it is highly protein-bound (96-99%).
